title: Capstone: Ship a Reusable Agent Workbench Pack

questions.question: What does the capstone produce?
options: A versioned drop-in directory with the seven surfaces plus an install.sh that runs idempotently
A detailed research paper summarizing the mini-track's findings for an academic audience
A brand-new fine-tuned model trained end to end on the workbench's own feedback records
A monitoring dashboard that graphs verification-gate pass rates across every branch of the repo over time
questions.explanation: The pack is the recipe; each install is a serving.

questions.question: Which is NOT part of the pack layout?
options: AGENTS.md and the docs/ directory that hold the pack's rules and rubric
The schemas/ directory that defines the pack's contract for target repos
vendor_proprietary_weights/, since the pack ships no model weights of its own
The scripts/ directory that supplies the pack's runtime behavior at install time
questions.explanation: Pack layout is AGENTS.md, docs/, schemas/, scripts/, bin/, README.md. The pack is framework- and vendor-agnostic.

questions.question: What does the lesson say bumps the pack's major version?
options: Any change at all, since the pack has no separate patch tier
Only changes to bin/install.sh, since it is the sole entry point
Adding a new doc file, since docs are the pack's main contract
Schema bumps and script changes that require a migration script
questions.explanation: The lesson says schema bumps and script changes that require migrations bump the major version, and doc-only changes bump the patch.

questions.question: What does the lesson say the installer refuses to do by default?
options: Copy the pack into a repo that has no .github/workflows/ directory
Run at all without an internet connection to fetch schema updates
Install into a repo where agent_state.json does not already exist
Install over an existing pack unless the operator passes --force
questions.explanation: The lesson lists the installer's first step as: refuses to install over an existing pack without --force.

questions.question: What three things does the lesson list as staying 'in' the pack?
options: The target repo's tasks, its CI secrets, and its onboarding wiki
A pinned model ID, a vendor SDK key, and a billing dashboard link
The installer log file, a changelog, and a support contact list
The surface schemas, the four scripts, and the four docs
questions.explanation: The lesson's 'what stays in' list is: surface schemas (the contract), the four scripts (the runtime), the four docs (the rules and the rubric).

questions.question: What stays OUT of the pack?
options: Surface schemas, since they are the only thing the installer copies into a target repo
Project-specific tasks, vendor SDK calls, and onboarding prose; the pack stays framework-agnostic
The four runtime scripts, since those alone define what the pack does at install time
The bin/install.sh entry point, since it is the single script a target repo directly and actually executes
questions.explanation: Tasks belong on the target repo's board, not the pack; vendor SDK calls would lock the pack to one framework.
